title: BFS and DFS Check
description: Predict traversal order and the queue-vs-stack difference between BFS and DFS.

questions.prompt: Which data structure does BFS use to decide which node to visit next?

options.text: A stack (LIFO)
A queue (FIFO)
A sorted array
A hash map

questions.explanation: BFS uses a queue: nodes are dequeued in the same order they were enqueued (FIFO), which produces level-by-level order.

questions.prompt: For adjacency list `[[1, 2], [3], [3], []]` starting at node `0`, what is the BFS visit order?
questions.explanation: BFS visits `0` first, enqueues `1` and `2` (its direct neighbors), then dequeues `1`, enqueues `3`, then dequeues `2` (already visited `3` is skipped), then dequeues `3` — giving `0, 1, 2, 3`.

questions.prompt: Why is BFS guaranteed to find the shortest path in an unweighted graph?

options.text: It visits nodes in alphabetical order
It visits all nodes at distance `k` before any node at distance `k+1`
It uses recursion, which is always optimal
It sorts edges by weight first

questions.explanation: BFS explores level by level (by number of edges from the start), so the first time it reaches a node is guaranteed to be via the fewest edges.

questions.prompt: What is the key structural difference between the BFS and DFS implementations shown in the lesson?

options.text: BFS uses `queue.shift()` (FIFO); DFS uses `stack.pop()` (LIFO) — everything else is the same
DFS does not need a `visited` set
BFS only works on trees, not graphs
DFS always runs faster than BFS

questions.explanation: Both implementations are structurally identical except for one operation: dequeue (FIFO) for BFS vs. pop (LIFO) for DFS.

questions.prompt: Why do both BFS and DFS mark a node as visited before or when adding it to the queue/stack?

options.text: To make the output alphabetically sorted
To avoid revisiting nodes and looping forever on a graph with cycles
It is optional and only affects performance slightly
To reduce memory usage of the adjacency list

questions.explanation: Without tracking visited nodes, a graph with a cycle would cause the traversal to revisit the same nodes forever.

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of both BFS and DFS on a graph with `V` vertices and `E` edges?

options.text: `O(log V)`

questions.explanation: Every vertex is visited once and every edge is examined once, giving `O(V + E)` for both traversals.
